rows.stem: A human ovum completes its second meiosis :

options.label: B
options.text: when the sperm touches the zona pellucida

options.label: C
options.text: when the sperm gains entry into the cytoplasm of the ovum

options.label: D
options.text: when the acrosome of the sperm releases its enzymes on corona radiata

rows.solution: In humans the secondary oocyte released at ovulation is arrested in meiosis II. During fertilisation a sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida layer of the ovum, which induces changes in the membrane that block the entry of additional sperms. It is the **entry of the sperm into the ovum (into its cytoplasm)** that induces the secondary oocyte to **complete its second meiotic division**. This is an unequal division: it produces the large haploid ovum (ootid) and a small **second polar body**. The haploid nuclei of the sperm and the ovum then fuse to form the diploid zygote. Contact with the zona pellucida and the acrosomal enzymes acting on the corona radiata come earlier and only help the sperm reach the ovum. So the answer is option (C) when the sperm gains entry into the cytoplasm of the ovum.

After the Human Genome Project, the genomes of several other organisms were sequenced, among them plants such as **rice** and Arabidopsis. Rice was the **first crop plant** whose genome was sequenced (a draft in 2002 and the finished sequence in 2005). It was chosen because it is a staple food crop with a relatively small genome among cereals, which makes it a model for the other grasses such as wheat and maize. So the answer is option (C) Rice.

rows.subtopic: Isolation, Cutting and Amplification of DNA
rows.stem:
Which of the following samples of DNA in the table given below will give the desired result during polymerase chain reaction ?
Sample, Temperature used for Denaturation, Enzyme used for extension
rows.solution:
In the polymerase chain reaction each cycle has three steps: **denaturation**, **annealing** of the primers and **extension**.
- **Denaturation** separates the two strands of the double-stranded DNA, which needs a **high temperature** (about \(90^{\circ}\text{C}\) to \(94^{\circ}\text{C}\)). At \(50^{\circ}\text{C}\) the strands would not separate.
- **Extension** is carried out by a **thermostable DNA polymerase** (Taq polymerase, isolated from the bacterium Thermus aquaticus), which stays active through the high temperatures of repeated denaturation. A heat-unstable enzyme would be destroyed in the first cycle.

Only sample I uses a high denaturation temperature together with a heat-stable enzyme, so only it gives the desired amplification. So the answer is option (A) I, High temp. / \(90^{\circ}\text{C}\), Heat stable.

rows.stem: Which one of the following is used during 'RNA i' process, to silence the desired gene ?
rows.solution: **RNA interference (RNAi)** is a method of cellular defence that takes place in all eukaryotic organisms. It involves the **silencing of a specific mRNA** by a complementary **double-stranded RNA (dsRNA)** molecule, which binds to the mRNA and prevents its translation. The source of this complementary RNA could be an infection by viruses having RNA genomes, or mobile genetic elements (transposons) that replicate via an RNA intermediate. In making tobacco plants resistant to the nematode Meloidogyne incognita, nematode-specific genes were introduced so that the host produced both sense and anti-sense RNA, forming dsRNA that silenced the specific mRNA of the nematode. So the answer is option (B) dsRNA.

rows.stem: Which one among the following biofertilizers does not fix atmospheric nitrogen ?
rows.solution:
- **Oscillatoria** is a cyanobacterium; many cyanobacteria fix atmospheric nitrogen and are used as biofertilisers in paddy fields.
- **Rhizobium** is a symbiotic bacterium that fixes atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of leguminous plants.
- **Azospirillum** is a free-living bacterium in the soil that fixes atmospheric nitrogen.
- **Glomus** is a **fungus** that forms **mycorrhiza** with the roots of plants. Its hyphae absorb **phosphorus** from the soil and pass it to the plant, and the association also gives resistance to root-borne pathogens and tolerance to salinity and drought. It does **not** fix nitrogen.

So the answer is option (D) Glomus.

rows.stem:
Examples that show commensalism are :
(i) An orchid growing on mango tree
(ii) Cuckoo bird and crow
(iii) Cuscuta growing on Nerium tree
(iv) Barnacles growing on a whale
rows.solution:
**Commensalism** is an interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited.
- (i) An **orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch** benefits from the support, while the mango tree derives no benefit and is not harmed: commensalism.
- (ii) The **cuckoo** lays its eggs in the **crow's nest** and lets the crow incubate them: this is **brood parasitism**, harmful to the crow.
- (iii) **Cuscuta** is a parasitic plant that draws its nutrition from the host: **parasitism**.
- (iv) **Barnacles growing on the back of a whale** benefit, while the whale derives no noticeable benefit: commensalism.

So the answer is option (B) (i) and (iv).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : A species of wasp and a fig species cannot complete their life cycle without each other.
Reason (R) : While visiting wasps come to lay eggs in the fig inflorescence, the flower of wasp gets pollinated in return.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The Assertion is true: many species of fig trees have a tight one-to-one relationship with the pollinator species of wasp, and neither partner can complete its life cycle without the other. A given fig species can be pollinated only by its 'partner' wasp species and no other species.

The Reason is also true and explains it: the **female wasp uses the fig fruit (the inflorescence) as an oviposition site** and the developing seeds within the fruit to nourish its larvae, while it **pollinates the fig inflorescence** in return as it searches for suitable egg-laying sites. This is a classic case of **mutualism**, each partner depending on the other. (The Reason as printed says "the flower of wasp"; the flowers pollinated are those of the fig.) So both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : For sequencing, the total DNA from a cell is isolated and converted into random fragments.
Reason (R) : DNA is a very long polymer.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The Assertion is true: in genome sequencing the method commonly used is to isolate the **total DNA from a cell** and convert it into **random fragments of relatively smaller sizes**, which are then sequenced using automated DNA sequencers.

The Reason is true and explains it: **DNA is a very long polymer**, and there are technical limitations in sequencing very long pieces of DNA. So it is first broken into small fragments, these are cloned in suitable hosts (using vectors such as BAC and YAC), sequenced, and the sequences are then arranged in order by finding the overlapping regions present in them. So both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : In order to cut the DNA with a restriction enzyme, it needs to be released from the membrane which encloses it.
Reason (R) : A plant cell was treated with chitinase to achieve this.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The Assertion is true: to cut DNA with restriction enzymes it must be in pure form, free from other macro-molecules, so it first has to be **released from the cell** by breaking the cell open, that is, by digesting the cell wall and the membranes that enclose it.

The Reason is false. The enzyme used depends on the cell type: a **plant cell** is treated with **cellulase** to break its cell wall, a **bacterial cell** with **lysozyme**, and a **fungal cell** with **chitinase**. Chitinase would not open a plant cell, whose wall is made of cellulose. So the Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
Assertion (A) : Darwin showed how even a slow growing animal like an elephant could reach enormous numbers.
Reason (R) : When resources in the habitat are unlimited, each species has the ability to realise its innate potential fully.
rows.context: For Questions number 13 to 16, two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer to these questions from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The Assertion is true: in the absence of checks, Darwin showed how even a **slow growing animal like an elephant** could reach enormous numbers over time. This illustrates **exponential growth**.

The Reason is true and explains it: when resources in the habitat are **unlimited**, each species has the ability to **realise fully its innate potential to grow in number**, as Darwin observed while developing his theory of natural selection. The population then grows in an exponential or geometric fashion, so given enough time even an animal that breeds slowly reaches enormous numbers. So both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
(a) Mention the main objective of the Ramsar Convention.
(b) Name any two sites in India that are important in the Ramsar Convention.
rows.solution:
(a) The main objective of the **Ramsar Convention** (signed at Ramsar, Iran, in 1971) is the **conservation and wise use of wetlands**, to stop the worldwide loss of wetlands, through national action and international cooperation.

(b) Any two of the many Ramsar sites in India, for example:
- **Chilika Lake** (Odisha)
- **Keoladeo National Park** (Rajasthan)
- **Ashtamudi Wetland** (Kerala)
- **Bhitarkanika Mangroves** (Odisha)
- **Bhoj Wetland** (Madhya Pradesh)
- **Chandra Taal** (Himachal Pradesh)

rows.stem:
(a) Why should antibiotics not be taken indiscriminately ? Give any two reasons.
(b) "It is advisable to complete the course of antibiotics as prescribed by the doctor." Justify.
rows.solution:
(a) Antibiotics should not be taken indiscriminately because:
- frequent and unnecessary use lets **antibiotic-resistant bacteria** survive and multiply faster than the susceptible ones, so infections become **resistant** and difficult to treat with ordinary antibiotics;
- antibiotics also kill the useful bacteria of the body (for example the gut flora), and taking them without need can cause side effects; resistant bacteria can also pass to humans through food chains.

(b) A course of antibiotics is designed to kill **all** the disease-causing bacteria. If it is stopped midway as soon as the patient feels better, some bacteria survive. These **surviving bacteria multiply**, the infection can come back, and the survivors are more likely to be **resistant** to the first-line drug, which raises the risk of complications and the cost of a longer illness. So the full course prescribed by the doctor must be completed.

rows.stem:
Study the pedigree chart of a family given below and answer the questions that follow :
(a) Is the disease in this pedigree chart a recessive or dominant disorder ? Give reason.
(b) Identify the female individual in this family, who for sure is homozygous.
(c) Genotype of which one individual cannot be identified in this pedigree chart ?
(d) Identify a male who is definitely heterozygous.
(e) Is this disease a sex-linked or an autosomal disorder ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED:a three-generation pedigree of circles and squares numbered 1 to 8: parents 1 (female) and 2 (male); their daughters 3 and 4; 4 married to 5 (male) with children 6 (male), 7 (male) and 8 (female). Which individuals are shaded decides every part, so it is withheld here. This pedigree differs from those of 57/1/1 Q23 and 57/1/2 Q28. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
(a) The disease is **recessive**. Individuals 1 and 2 do not have the disease, yet their daughter 3 shows it. The allele must have been carried by both unaffected parents and passed to individual 3; a dominant disorder would have been expressed in at least one of them. (Individuals 4 and 5, both unaffected, having an affected son 6 point the same way.)

(b) **Individual 3** is the female who is surely homozygous: she shows a recessive disorder, which is expressed only in the homozygous condition (aa).

(c) **Individual 7 (or individual 8)**. Their parents 4 and 5 must both be carriers (Aa), since they have an affected son 6, so an unaffected child of theirs may be either AA or Aa, and the chart cannot tell which. (Both 7 and 8 are in this position, so the marking scheme accepts either.)

(d) **Individual 2 (or individual 5)** is a male who is definitely heterozygous (Aa): each is unaffected yet has fathered an affected child (2 is the father of 3, and 5 is the father of 6), so each must carry one recessive allele.

(e) It is an **autosomal disorder**. A sex-linked (X-linked) recessive disorder in a daughter needs the allele on both her X chromosomes, one of which comes from her father, so her father would also be affected. Here the affected daughter 3 has an unaffected father 2, which rules out X-linkage.

rows.stem:
(i) Describe the phenomenon of adaptive radiation as explained by Darwin.
(ii) Is human evolution an example of adaptive radiation ? Give reason in support of your answer.
You are given a tall pea plant and asked to determine its genotype. Name and explain the cross that you will carry out to find the possible genotype of the given tall pea plant.
rows.solution:
The cross to carry out is a **test cross**: the tall plant whose genotype is unknown is crossed with a **recessive parent**, a pure **dwarf** plant (tt).

A tall pea plant can have the genotype **TT** (homozygous dominant) or **Tt** (heterozygous), because the allele for tallness (T) is dominant over the allele for dwarfness (t), and both look alike. The dwarf parent can only give gametes carrying t, so the phenotypes of the progeny reveal the alleles carried by the tall plant.

**Case I: the tall plant is TT.**
- Parents: TT \(\times\) tt
- Gametes: T only, and t only
- Progeny: all Tt

All the plants of this cross are **tall (100% tall)**.

**Case II: the tall plant is Tt.**
- Parents: Tt \(\times\) tt
- Gametes: T and t, and t only
- Progeny: Tt and tt in the ratio 1 : 1

Half the plants are **tall** and half are **dwarf (50% tall : 50% dwarf)**.

So if all the progeny are tall, the given plant is homozygous (TT); if dwarf plants appear in about a 1 : 1 ratio with tall ones, it is heterozygous (Tt).
